findings.title: The redelivery case was green without a redelivery
findings.mechanism: The batch completes inside an acknowledgement window the broker actually supports. RabbitMQ documents that the timeout is evaluated at one minute intervals and that values below one minute are not supported, so the endpoint asks for 60000 ms; the delivered spec asked for 10000 ms and would have asserted a window the broker never applied.

proof.counters: deliveries=2, firstDiscarded=True, effects=3, one per message, ready=0, unacked=0
proof.broker: the run's own broker log carries 'has timed out waiting for a consumer acknowledgement … Timeout used: 60000 ms'
proof.removed: The assertion on probe.Faults is gone together with its collection and method. Nothing ever filled it, so it was green by construction; record 0039 was right to reject it.

findings.title: The setup error of the test harness was swallowed
findings.mechanism: Both close sites log the original failure at error level, close best effort inside their own guard, and rethrow bare so the stack of the throw site survives.
findings.proof: Four specs and four mutations: removing the rethrow turns three red; replacing it with 'throw ex' turns the stack spec red; leaving the close reason untrimmed changes nothing on its own, and only rethrowing the close failure as well changes the outcome — which is what proves the close really ran and really failed in the row before.

findings.title: The job service lifecycle had no owner
findings.mechanism: Stop and BusStarted run under one gate. Admission is a single decision under the same lock Stop takes, and a job admitted but not yet registered counts as outstanding for the drain. The heartbeat belongs to the generation that created it: an owned loop with cancellation and an awaitable end, so Stop returns only once its publication has finished.
findings.proof: Twelve specs, seven mutations. The two lifecycle defects named by record 0045 are each caught by their own deterministic race spec: one synchronises between the stopping check and the registration, the other inside a blocked heartbeat publication.

findings.title: The exclusivity conflict proved its own timeout
delivered: RESOURCE_LOCKED 405 is classified as permanent in all three shapes it arrives in, and only on a real reply code — every search in broker prose was removed.
The already-closed channel exception carries the broker's unaltered ShutdownEventArgs, proved by a direct producer test whose mutation is caught.
A clean up failure never replaces the primary exception, proved by five transport neutral specs and their mutation.
The provenance of a locally disposed channel is no longer reported as a peer answer.
Fixed delays in both exclusivity fixtures are replaced by an observable broker condition with an upper bound.
findings.open: Under load the conflict still reaches the caller after 33 to 60 seconds instead of within the bound 20. The one measurement ordered by record 0052 ruled out the fan-out hypothesis for this endpoint — ConfigureTopology starts exactly one queue task — and established the intended chain across all seven stations, but it did not reproduce the failure. Naming the loss point in the failing case needs a measurement frame that produces it, which is the lead's decision.
findings.notClaimed: Nothing here asserts F-3 as closed. Two earlier causal statements of mine were withdrawn after the bound broker evidence contradicted them.
